Indy games are getting a lot of skeptical inquiry because of gamergate. The things is, the indy scene never was. Or rather, it's always been disparate groups that got lumped together.

"Ethics in journalism", as shouted from the rooftops, is a response to many things. Reviewers were getting overly cozy with big publishers "IGN: game only prints HELLO WORLD, 9.5 stars!", gaming outlets trading influence, and a general contempt for the customer from both publishers and media.

A lot of the influence peddling was used to promote the pink hair crowd of indy development. Folks that figured out that coding a 2d game (or zero d, like ZQ) using existing tools and libraries wasn't super difficult anymore. That particular niche happened to appeal to a lot of folks for reasons that only briefly intersected with the SJW crowd. I'm old, I loved the side scrolling coin-ops of my youth. Folks looked at the market response and drew the wrong conclusions. "Gamers are dead! Players want progressive culture! Computing power doesn't matter anymore!" Not so much. I liked most of Braid because of the flat game play, not the male-guilt story line.

Do what you love. I get excited about new mechanics and positively giddy when I see something really clever. Triple A titles can't afford to be innovative anymore, for the same reasons that big movie studios can't afford not to re-make everything successful over and over again.

Just because you're off doing your own thing doesn't mean that you will be held accountable for the pink hair crowd. Do something clever, invest your time in what you want to do, and it'll go fine. Love your customers, give them something worth playing.

I'm not a dev but I'll comment regardless.

Friend, you hold your head up high and you make whatever the hell you want. Someone I highly respect said that, in response to the flames surrounding all this, all you gotta do is just create. It's not just the waters that will douse the flames surrounding this controversy, it's also the water that will revitalize you. Focus, don't let others sap your drive, and once your game's out there, promote it and be proud of it, and eff any cliques who want to keep you down.
